A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlowState and retain the same core research identity. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison throughout. v1 ends after its references; v3 additionally contains Appendices A–D, which were inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original FlowState evaluations on GIFT-ZS, full GIFT-Eval and Chronos-ZS, plus sampling-rate robustness experiments and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, expanded ablations, mixed-rate forecasting demonstrations, representation analyses and scale-selection experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The SSM encoder, functional basis decoder and parallel-forecast training remain central. v3 adds an explicit output gate to the SSM block equations and architecture diagram, and Appendix D.2.2 introduces an optional automatic seasonality/scale-selection procedure. These are localized procedural extensions.

E1.justification: Coverage is substantially reworked: the separate Chronos-ZS evaluation disappears, and the resampling study switches from Loop Seattle traffic to ETT temperature data. v3 adds hourly-context-to-15-minute-target forecasting and synthetic sine-wave tests with seasonalities 8, 24 and 100. Full GIFT-Eval was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: The full GIFT-Eval comparison replaces TimesFM-2.0 and Chronos-bolt-b with TimesFM-2.5 and Chronos-2-Synth, adds Kairos-23M/50M, and drops TabPFN-TS and YingLong. Appendix A.1 introduces comparisons with LightGTS-mini, MOIRAI-L, iTransformer and PatchTST. The robustness experiment also changes its comparator membership.

E3.justification: Reported main-model context increases from 2048 to 4096 steps, base forecasting length changes from 24 to 6, and model sizes change from 2.6M/9.1M to 3M/10.6M/18.6M. Synthetic generation changes from KernelSynth to CauKer. v3 also introduces four-horizon MSE/MAE evaluation in Appendix A.1 and changes the resampling study's intervals and MAE normalization.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands ablations to test output gating, real versus complex SSMs, selective step sizes, a fixed decoder, time noise, causal normalization and basis truncation. Appendices add decoder case studies, aligned/misaligned encoding comparisons, automatic scale selection and scale sensitivity. v1's CPM/MPI ablations are removed.

E5.justification: v1 provides no run-count or variability estimates. v3 Table 2 newly reports a three-seed baseline with MASE and CRPS standard deviations of 0.0007 and 0.0011. Appendix D.1's blanket statement that all experiments ran once with seed 0 conflicts with this account; repeated-run coverage beyond that baseline remains unclear.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. Full GIFT-Eval reports FlowState(G)-9.1M at 0.738 MASE/0.508 CRPS in v1 Table 3, versus the newly configured FlowState-18.6M at 0.701/0.487 in v3 Table 1; this is not a controlled same-setting gain. Chronos-ZS results disappear, while standard-benchmark, expanded-ablation and scale-selection results are added.

T1.justification: v1 offers architectural equations and informal sampling-rate arguments. v3 Section 4 and Appendix B add formal approximate equivariance, input-Lipschitz and exponential-stability assumptions, a two-rate ZOH mismatch proposition and proof, decoder error bounds, and a conditional multilayer extension.

C1.justification: The headline claim changes from state of the art on GIFT-ZS and Chronos-ZS to state of the art on full GIFT-Eval. For full GIFT-Eval, v1 only claimed leadership among models without test-data leakage and approximate parity with TiRex overall. v3 also makes end-to-end sampling-rate equivariance an explicit central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of fixed-decoder local errors, complex-state dependence, time-noise regularization and basis truncation. New limitations identify heuristic scale selection and absent native multivariate/covariate support; Appendix D discusses automatic-selection failures with short contexts. The theoretical discussion qualifies equivariance as approximate and assumption-dependent.

D1.justification: v3 adds a FlowState model-access link and extensive reproducibility information in Appendices C–D: dataset inventories, balancing and preprocessing, augmentation details, quantile loss, optimizer and training hyperparameters, seasonality-selection pseudocode, model dimensions, hardware and training times. Most of this information is absent from v1.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and connections to Chronos-2, Kairos, LightGTS, CauKer, diagonal-SSM initialization and classical discretization theory. The broader positioning relative to transformers, MLPs, SSMs and HiPPO remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title and sampling-rate terminology, numbers sections, separates parallel forecasting from the architecture section, and rewrites the experimental narrative. Much of the introduction, background and core-method explanation remains closely matched; the largest expansion consists of new scientific and technical material.

P2.justification: v3 updates the architecture diagram, replaces the robustness plot with different axes and normalization, restructures the benchmark and ablation tables, and adds mixed-rate forecasts, decoder case-study plots, encoding heatmaps, a sensitivity plot and technical tables. The original parallel-training schematic is retained as Figure 3. Appendices introduce a substantial single-column presentation.

improvement.justification: v1's central sampling-rate argument was largely informal and its training documentation sparse. v3 substantially strengthens the paper through conditional error bounds, direct decoder ablations, scale-selection and sensitivity analyses, explicit limitations and detailed reproducibility information. Removed Chronos-ZS coverage, less explicit overlap safeguards and inconsistent seed reporting are drawbacks, but the stronger support for the central mechanism and improved documentation provide a substantial net gain.
